notes: Migrated on 2026-11-11 to the current layout: the indeterminate queries and worlds were removed (TBox records have determinate derived queries only), a third propositional query was added (negation, conjunction with a true side fact, disjunction with a false one) and each derived query now names its task, fact and derivability with evidence. TBox rule edit. Derivability very_unlikely: needing a material medium is what defines a mechanical wave (Wikipedia), stated in general form in teaching texts ("mechanical waves need a medium" 89, "mechanical wave" 26,235); it follows from nothing more basic. Counterfactual: clearly false, and a common student confusion of mechanical with electromagnetic waves. A reviewer noted (angle) that this edits a definition rather than a contingent class rule; that holds for most TBox rules in this topic and is kept, as the dataset's TBox edits are class rules of this kind. The paraphrase now has the same polarity as the direct question (both "no" before the edit), after two models answered the reversed form wrongly (REFINEMENTS). Derived queries name made-up wave kinds (Halvorsen ripple, Teague wave, Ardell wave) known only by their class (inheritance, 2 hops); the Teague question is an application (signalling between spacecraft) and states no answer. Sound is not used: its own need for a medium is stored by name, which would make its answer indeterminate. Near query changed (it was a units question an over-applied edit could not touch): which medium sound crosses fastest (steel), a neighbouring fact about how a mechanical wave travels through media, unaffected by the vacuum rule and different from the new answer.
